subject: EU residency & APAC latency: proposed hosting fallback and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Moreno <anna@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25 09:15 -0400
Subject: Quick recap + requested info (data residency & APAC latency)

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks.

Summary of requirements you mentioned:
- Primary requirement: All PHI and patient-identifiable inference traffic must be stored and processed in the EU (Ireland data center).
- APAC user population: latency-sensitive web customers in Singapore/Japan — want sub-150ms tail latency for UI prompts if possible.
- Procurement: you need an outline of options (cost + SLA) and a short draft SOW to share with legal.
- Questions raised on call: cross-region fallbacks (if EU Dedicated is unavailable, can APAC edge handle non-PHI queries?), KMS/HSM key residency, and audit/log retention windows for SOC2.

Our suggested next steps (pending your confirmation):
1) We prepare a 2-week pilot proposal: Dedicated EU capacity for PHI workloads + hosted APAC edge cache for latency-sensitive non-PHI inference.
2) Internal security checklist: confirm KMS integration options (customer-managed keys in EU) and retention windows for audit logs.
3) Draft SOW v1 for procurement with pricing ranges for Dedicated vs Private VPC.

Attached: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (short matrix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private + pros/cons for EU/APAC), and a pointer to our example SOW.

Could you confirm two quick items: (a) whether any APAC traffic must be stored in-region (not just cached), and (b) an expected timeline for procurement review?

If that's aligned, we can aim to have the pilot SOW and a proposed timeline by EOW (Oct 30).

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Subject: Re: Quick recap + requested info (data residency & APAC latency)

Thanks Vanessa — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: Yes, all PHI must remain and be processed in the EU. Non-PHI inference may be served from regional caches, but we need guarantees that no PHI leaves EU boundaries (including logs and KV cache).
- APAC: We do not require persistent storage in APAC for PHI; the ask is strictly low-latency observation (UI response) for local users.
- Procurement timing: aiming to take vendor shortlists to procurement by Nov 10; legal will need a short SOW + security annex.

Two more questions for your engineers: (1) If Dedicated EU is fully utilized, how does Redwood handle overflow? Is there an automatic fallback to hosted API in another region, or would that require manual escalation? (2) Can we get a short write-up on how KMS keys are stored and rotated if we use a customer-managed key?

I've attached a simple dataflow diagram we sketched out (lumos-dataflow-diagram.png) that shows our current traffic patterns.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Anna
Head of Platform — Lumos Health
anna@lumoshealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26 09:40 -04:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + requested info (data residency & APAC latency)

Folks — notes from a quick technical triage I drafted after reviewing Anna's diagram:

Short answer: We can meet Lumos' constraints with a hybrid approach that minimizes risk and avoids an expensive full on-prem Private deployment up front. Proposed pattern:
- Primary: Dedicated EU capacity (isolated GPU pool in Ireland) for all PHI inference. This keeps storage, inference, and logs in-region.
- APAC tail latency: Hosted APAC edge nodes provide a regional KV cache + routing layer. Non-PHI traffic (or sanitized prompts) get served from APAC edges to hit <150ms.
- Overflow policy: By default we keep traffic in-region; if EU Dedicated saturates, fallback options are: (a) queue/auto-scale EU Dedicated (preferred), (b) burst to EU-hosted spare capacity (same region but different pool), (c) only with customer authorization, allow non-PHI requests to use APAC-hosted variants. We should capture the fallback strategy and an opt-in toggle in the SOW.

Security/KMS: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) via our KMS integration; keys can be provisioned and stored in the customer's EU KMS (we do not hold plaintext). Key rotation and HSM-backed operations are supported — will provide a 1-page KMS tech note.

Action items for the next 48 hours:
- Vanessa: send draft SOW with the fallback opt-in language and cost bands (Dedicated EU + APAC edge).
- Grace: produce the 1-page KMS note and SOC2 retention summary (logs retention and access patterns).
- Me: prepare a quick cost estimate for a 3-month pilot (reserved Dedicated nodes + edge traffic estimate).

I recommend we avoid recommending Private VPC/on-prem at this stage unless Lumos specifically requires that no inference compute ever leaves their network — that is a heavier lift operationally and procurement will likely take longer.

Karthik
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Moreno <anna@lumoshealth.com>, Procurement Team <procure@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26 11:05 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + requested info (data residency & APAC latency)

Anna / Procurement — thanks for the quick answers. Based on the call and Karthik's notes below, here's what we'd like to propose as a near-term plan and the asks from Lumos to move forward: 

Proposed near-term pilot (timeline and deliverables):
- Scope: 8-week pilot using Dedicated EU capacity for PHI workloads + hosted APAC edge for non-PHI low-latency responses.
- Deliverables: SOW v1 (attached) + security annex, 1-page KMS note, cost estimate for a 3-month reserved window.
- Fallback behavior: EU Dedicated auto-scale first; if capacity constraints persist, we will queue and notify Lumos. Any cross-region fallback to APAC-hosted inference will require explicit Lumos opt-in. We will include a toggle in the console/SOW.
- Timeline: draft SOW & annex to you by Oct 30; procurement review target Nov 10; pilot start target Nov 20 (subject to PO).

Requested confirmations from Lumos:
1) Confirm that the fallback opt-in approach is acceptable (default: no cross-region PHI processing).
2) Confirm procurement timeline and the primary procurement contact (I see procure@lumoshealth.com — is there a legal reviewer we should email the SOW to?).

Next steps from our side (internal): Grace will send the KMS note and SOC2 log-retention summary by EOD today; Karthik will send the cost bands. I'll circulate SOW v1 to Procurement and copy legal.

Forwarding the original call notes below for context.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
